description: We are friends from Tanta University of engineering, we are willing to take this opportunity to learn more about space and robotics, while trying this new experience to learn as much as we can
summary:
HORIZON X built MESIS (Martian Exploration & Survival Intelligence System) for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 in Giza, under the “Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map” challenge. It’s an interactive Mars map: you click any point and see every scientific measurement available for that spot, with the source and how reliable it is.

The problem it solves: Picking where to land, build or explore on Mars means checking thin air, radiation, dust storms, terrain, water ice and resources. The data for each of these is spread across different NASA, USGS and university archives, in different formats and resolutions. MESIS brings them together in one place.
details:
What it does: MESIS is an interactive Mars map. Click any point and it shows every available scientific measurement for that spot, with its source and a reliability label. It also ranks landing and base sites for 7 mission types and compares routes (safest, shortest, science, resources) by distance, time, climb and hazards.

Benefits: It puts 22 NASA and partner datasets in one place instead of dozens of separate archives. It uses no synthetic data, so missing values stay missing and modeled values are labelled. Users can see why a site or route was chosen, and it works in English and Arabic on desktop and mobile.

Impact: It helps planners, scientists and students decide where to go on Mars and how to get there safely. In one example, the safest route was only 4% longer than the shortest but about 10 sols faster, with three times less climbing.

Tools: We wrote it in Python (NumPy, Pillow, Matplotlib) and TypeScript with React, using esbuild and a custom canvas map built for Mars coordinates. Testing used Playwright and Python unittest, with all 52 automated checks passing. The data comes from MOLA, TES, Mars Odyssey, SWIM, the USGS geologic map, the Robbins & Hynek crater database, and Curiosity and Perseverance mission data. It runs on standard laptops in any browser.

Creativity: MESIS turns maps into survival decisions, labels every value with its source and status, and runs on a map built for Mars rather than Earth. It is also bilingual for our local community.

Factors considered: We weighed scientific accuracy, transparency about data limits, crew safety (terrain, radiation, dust, ice, thin atmosphere) and performance. We also state the platform's limits: 7.4 km terrain cells, indirect ice evidence away from the poles, and no gridded temperature or dust data yet.
